before.title: The p=1 Gagliardo-Nirenberg-Sobolev inequality
before.statement: Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$. There is a constant $C(n)$ such that $\|u\|_{L^{n/(n-1)}(\mathbb R^n)}\le C(n)\,\|Du\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^n)}$ for every $u\in C_c^{\infty}(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$.
before.strategy: For each $j$ the fundamental theorem of calculus and compact support give $|u(x)|\le\int_{\mathbb R}|\partial_ju(x_1,\dots,t,\dots,x_n)|\,dt$ for every $x$. Multiply the $n$ pointwise inequalities and take the $(n-1)$-th root: $|u(x)|^{n/(n-1)}\le\prod_{j=1}^n\big(\int_{\mathbb R}|\partial_ju|\,dt_j\big)^{1/(n-1)}$. Integrate successively over $x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n$; at step $j$ apply the generalized Hölder inequality to the product of the $n-1$ remaining factors, each of which is an $L^1$ function of the free variables; Tonelli's theorem justifies the iterated integrals. The result is $\|u\|_{n/(n-1)}^{n/(n-1)}\le\prod_j\int_{\mathbb R^n}|Du|=\|Du\|_1^{n/(n-1)}$.

before.title: The Poincare inequality for zero-boundary Sobolev closures on domains bounded in one direction
before.statement: Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and bounded in one direction: there are a unit vector $e$ and $a<b$ with $a<x\cdot e<b$ for every $x\in\Omega$. Let $1\le p<\infty$. Then $\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C(p)\,(b-a)\,\|Du\|_{L^p(\Omega)}$ for every $u\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega;\mathbb K)$.
before.strategy: Rotate so that $e=e_n$ and $\Omega\subset\{a<x_n<b\}$. For $u\in C_c^{\infty}(\Omega)$, the fundamental theorem in the $x_n$ direction and compact support give $|u(x)|\le\int_a^b|\partial_nu(x',t)|dt$; Hölder gives $|u(x)|^p\le(b-a)^{p-1}\int_a^b|\partial_nu(x',t)|^pdt$. Integrate over $\Omega$, extend the $x_n$-integral over $(a,b)$ for each $x'$ and apply Tonelli: $\|u\|_p^p\le(b-a)^p\|Du\|_p^p$. The full class follows because $C_c^{\infty}(\Omega)$ is dense in $W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)$ by definition and both sides are continuous in the $W^{1,p}$-norm. The factor $2\operatorname{diam}$-type constants of the general statements are not needed here; boundedness in one direction suffices.

before.title: Sobolev embedding on bounded extension domains for $p<n$
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded $W^{1,p}$-extension domain with a bounded extension operator $E$, and let $1\le p<n$, $p\le q\le p^{*}=\frac{np}{n-p}$. Then $W^{1,p}(\Omega)\hookrightarrow L^q(\Omega)$ continuously:
$$\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C(n,p,q,\Omega)\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}\qquad(u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)).$$
before.strategy: Let $W=Eu$. The whole-space inequality [[thm-gagliardo-nirenberg-sobolev-inequality]] applied to $W$ gives $\|W\|_{L^{p^{*}}(\mathbb R^n)}\le C\|DW\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}\le C\|E\|\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}$; restricting to $\Omega$ and applying the transfer corollary gives the endpoint case $q=p^{*}$. For $p\le q\le p^{*}$ write $1/q=\theta/p+(1-\theta)/p^{*}$ with $\theta\in[0,1]$; Hölder on the finite-measure set $\Omega$ gives $\|u\|_q\le\|u\|_p^{\theta}\|u\|_{p^{*}}^{1-\theta}\le C\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}$, since $\|u\|_p\le\|u\|_{W^{1,p}}$. Every bounded $C^k$ domain, $k\ge1$, supplies an admissible $E$ through the extension theorem cited in the transfer corollary.

references.locator: Chapter 3 §3.6, Definition 3.42 and Theorem 3.43 with proof, printed pp. 84–85.

before.title: Weak partial derivatives lower the Sobolev order
before.statement: Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $k\ge1$, $1\le p\le\infty$ and $u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. For every multi-index $\beta$ with $|\beta|\le k$ the weak derivative $D^{\beta}u$, viewed as an $L^p$ class, belongs to $W^{k-|\beta|,p}(\Omega)$, and $D^{\alpha}(D^{\beta}u)=D^{\alpha+\beta}u$ a.e. whenever $|\alpha|+|\beta|\le k$.
before.strategy: For $k=1$ and $|\beta|=1$, $D^{\beta}u\in L^p$ by definition and its weak derivative in a further coordinate direction $e_j$ is $D^{\beta+e_j}u$: the defining integration-by-parts identity for $D^{\beta+e_j}u$ is exactly the identity for the class $D^{\beta}u$ tested against $\partial_j\varphi$, by the commutation and locality properties of weak derivatives. Uniqueness of weak derivatives makes the construction representative-independent. The general case is induction on $k$ using this single step.

references.locator: Chapter 1 §1.2, Definition 1.8, printed pp. 4–5; §1.3, Lemma 1.14(2) and proof, printed pp. 9–10, for iterated weak derivatives.

before.title: Higher-order Sobolev embedding
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega$ be a bounded $W^{k,p}$-extension domain, $k\ge1$ and $1\le p<\infty$. Then:

1. if $kp<n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every $q$ with $\frac1q\ge\frac1p-\frac kn$ (equivalently $1\le q\le\frac{np}{n-kp}$);
2. if $kp=n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C(q)\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every finite $q$;
3. if $kp>n$, then for every integer $m\ge0$ and every $0<\alpha<1$ with $m+\alpha<k-\frac np$ there is a representative in $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ with $\|u\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$; when $k-\frac np\notin\mathbb Z$ one may take $m=\lfloor k-\frac np\rfloor$ and $\alpha=k-\frac np-m$.

Here $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ uses the continuous derivatives of the constructed representative on an ambient neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega$, with norm
$$\|g\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}:=\sum_{|\beta|\le m}\sup_{\overline\Omega}|D^\beta g|+\sum_{|\beta|=m}\sup_{\substack{x,y\in\overline\Omega\\x\ne y}}\frac{|D^\beta g(x)-D^\beta g(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha}.$$
For $\Omega=\varnothing$ set these norm values to $0$. The proof supplies such an ambient representative, so no boundary differentiability or regularity of $\partial\Omega$ is assumed.
before.strategy: Iterate the first-order whole-space Sobolev inequality on a compactly supported W^{k,p} extension. In the supercritical case, descend derivative order while increasing the exponent until q>=n; if q>n, Morrey on a fixed ambient ball gives a closure-wide representative, with extra remaining derivatives allowing any larger finite q. If q=n, at least two derivatives remain and compact support plus Holder reduces w and Dw to W^{1,s} for s<n near n, after which Gagliardo-Nirenberg-Sobolev gives a supercritical exponent. Mollification proves consistency of the continuous derivative representatives.

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Sobolev Spaces (Aalto University, 2026, complete graduate lecture notes)
references.locator: Chapter 3 §3.5, Remark 3.41 and its iteration argument, printed pp. 83–84; §3.3, Theorem 3.23 and Remarks 3.25, printed pp. 75–77, for the first-order Morrey input.

references.title: Gerald Teschl, Partial Differential Equations: From Classical to Modern (archived 2025 author manuscript)

before.title: The Hilbert transform of an $H^1$ atom is integrable
before.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n\ge1$ and let $a$ be a $(1,\infty,0)$-atom supported in a compact cube
$Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n$. Let $T$ be the Hilbert transform when $n=1$
([[def-truncated-hilbert-transform-and-principal-value]]) and the vector
$(R_1,\dots,R_n)$ of Riesz transforms when $n\ge2$
([[def-riesz-transforms-on-euclidean-space]]); each component is an $L^2$-bounded Calderon-Zygmund operator by [[lem-hilbert-and-riesz-transforms-are-calderon-zygmund-operators]] with a standard Holder kernel whose
constants are bounded by dimensional multiples of $1$
([[lem-riesz-transform-kernels-have-explicit-size-difference-and-spherical-cancellation-bounds]]).
Then every component $Ta$ lies in $L^1(\mathbb R^n)$ and
$$\|Ta\|_{L^1}\le C_n(A_1+A_2'+A_3+B),$$
where $A_1,A_2',A_3,B$ are the kernel size, Holder, cancellation and $L^2$
constants of the component. Write $\ell=\ell(Q)$ and let $Q^\dagger$ be the
concentric cube of side length $2\sqrt n\,\ell$. The near/far split is
explicit:
$$\int_{Q^\dagger}|Ta|\le|Q^\dagger|^{1/2}\|Ta\|_{L^2}\le(2\sqrt n)^{n/2}B,\qquad \int_{(Q^\dagger)^c}|Ta|\le C_{n,\delta}A_2'\|a\|_{L^1}\le C_{n,\delta}A_2',$$
the far estimate using only the zeroth moment of $a$ and the Holder bound for
the kernel.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: Proposition 7.35 and its proof, printed pp. 40-41: the complete near/far estimate for an atom

references.locator: Theorem 1.4(1), printed pp. 15-16: uniformly bounded atom images for regular singular integral operators
